subject: SLA uplift & capacity onramp for renewal — premium support addendum
messages:
From: Alex Wang <alex.wang@skylinehealth.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@skylinehealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions — premium SLA and committed throughput

Ben,

We’re starting renewal prep for Skyline Health (contract end 2027-09-30) and want to discuss upgrading to Redwood’s Premium SLA and reserving additional committed capacity for Q4. A few asks up front:

- Can you confirm the 99th pct latency SLO you’d guarantee for the new plan (current production median is ~120ms for our prompts; tail latency spikes during end-of-month ETL windows).
- What committed capacity increments do you recommend for our profile? We saw a ~2.8x spike during our last marketing campaign. I attached our Q2 usage export.
- Any options for a 30–60 day canary before the full upsell goes live? We want rollback & fallbacks defined in writing.

We’ll need pricing and a procurement timeline to align with our finance/IT approvals. Priya is copied for procurement.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Wang
Director of Platform Engineering
Skyline Health

Attachments:
- usage_report_Q2.csv (attachment)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wang <alex.wang@skylinehealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — premium SLA and committed throughput

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file. Appreciated. High level response below; I’ll coordinate a one-hour sync to run numbers with your infra team next week.

Quick answers:
- 99th pct latency SLO: We can offer a 99th percentile token latency SLO of 250ms for your current generation profile on Premium SLA with a dedicated routing policy and prefix caching enabled. If you elect dedicated capacity (reserved pool) and agree to the proposed commit tier, we can tighten to 180–200ms 99th pct — Evelyn can confirm the engineering tradeoffs.
- Committed capacity: Based on the spike profile in Q2, recommending a committed capacity uplift of 2.5x with a 1.5x burst window for seasonal peaks; this balances cost and headroom.
- Canary: We support a staged canary (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic fallback to your existing model variant and region-level routing. We’ll document rollback criteria (error rate >1.5% or latency breach >2 consecutive hours) and include it in the addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal ops feasibility check (Evelyn) and pricing draft (Camila).
2) 30–45 min technical call with your infra + Priya to confirm peak shaping and canary plan.
3) We’ll send a draft SLA addendum + DocuSign link for signature and a procurement checklist for your finance team.

I’m copying Marissa (CS lead) and Camila (sales ops) to align on credits and procurement timeline. Can you do Wed 4 Aug 10am PT?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — premium SLA and committed throughput

Alex — glad you flagged the ETL window spikes. A few commercial / operational notes from our side: 

- We can provide a one-time onboarding credit for the first 60 days of the committed capacity uplift (up to $25k) to smooth sizing risk; happy to include this in the redline if you need it for finance approval.
- For canary + rollback: CS will run the alerting & playbook handoff at 50% traffic. If your ops team wants a dry-run week where we simulate the traffic ramp (no billing changes), we can do that to validate network and caching behavior.
- Can we aim to have the SLA addendum signed and procurement PO issued by 2027-08-26 to meet a Q4 onramp? Camila — please prepare the pricing worksheet and the procurement checklist.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Wang <alex.wang@skylinehealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — premium SLA and committed throughput

Ben / Alex — technical addendum from infra: 

- 99th pct targets are conditional on model configuration (sequence length distribution) and KV cache hit rate. For Skyline’s typical prompts (~120 tokens median), targeted 99th pct of 200ms is realistic on dedicated RTX-class pools with continuous batching and prefix caching. If your long prompts (>512 tokens) are >10% of traffic, expect tail to widen; advise token cap guidance or prompt truncation for canary.
- Autoscaling & burst: We recommend 1.5x committed burst via short-lived transient workers; this requires a 48-hour advance notice window for large planned events >3x normal traffic.
- Oncall: We’ll allocate two dedicated SRE rotations during the 2-week ramp window to reduce MTTD and coordinate with Skyline’s oncall.

I’ll attach the earlier internal runbook and then we can convert relevant sections into the SLA addendum.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Infrastructure Reliability | Redwood Inference
